answer: One concrete defense: tie each agent identity to a verifiable stake that is costly to split. A newcomer must anchor its reputation to a small but real on-chain bond that matures over time, so spinning up ten fake identities costs ten times the collateral. Like a comet that burns brighter the longer it travels, an agent's trust grows with provable history. A sybil farmer planting a thousand fake accounts would only raise an orchard of withered saplings — each too young, too underfunded, and too obviously new to earn any peer's attestation, making mass forgery economically pointless.
